newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end down on peso fright.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end down on peso fright.

text.p: Mexican stocks reversed early gains and fell on Friday as dealers took fright over the weakening peso and stepped out of equities.
"The peso's slide kept foreign investors on the sidelines while they wait to see where it ends up," said Esteban Rojas, deputy research director at the Arka brokerage.
"Also, the market feels that domestic interest rates have bottomed out and will have to increase at next week's primary auction."
The IPC index closed off 30.20 points, or 0.90 percent, at 3,335.15 percent. The peso closed 6.1 centavos off at 7.6800 in key 48-hour contracts.

Other traders pointed out that the peso may have slid due to mounting pressure in recent weeks from commentators to the effect that the peso had stood still against the dollar for almost a year, and export companies were thus losing their competitive edge.
"It was like a pressure cooker ... it's better that we have a gradual slide between now and December than a sudden last-minute jolt," said one peso trader.

The bolsa's late decline shunned the trend set by the Dow Jones industrial average, which closed up a bullish 47.71 points, or 0.81 percent, at 5.969.38 as news that wholesale prices edged up only slightly last month helped the market to overcome worries about upcoming corporate earnings.
The IPC itself reached an early gain of 3,377.41 points.
Other traders pointed out that prospects for stocks were not bad, and that the slide was on thin volume.
"Jitters were present today, but sales volume was thin, there just weren't any buyers," said a floor trader.
Volume was a reasonable 92.97 million shares, but was exaggerated by two trades totalling almost 26 million shares.
Stock trading was meanwhile very selective with companies beginning to report earnings, Rojas added.

Mining company San Luis opened the reporting season with earnings that were well received by the market. The stock gained 1.4 pesos (18 cents) to 42.00 pesos ($5.47), the second highest percentage gain of the day.
"San Luis went down well, the stock rebounded immediately," a trader said.
Losers were headed by autoparts firm Iasasa B series -- down 4 centavos (1 cent) to 42 centavos (5 cents) -- which had not traded for seven months until Thursday.
